questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Some people judge a town by its tall buildings and wide roads. The writer of this article does not agree. For him, a good town is a town that takes care of its weakest people: its children, its old people and its sick."

What is the writer's main point?

options.text: A good town cares about its weakest people.
Tall buildings make a town rich and beautiful.
Towns should build wider roads for their cars.
Children, old and sick people live in every town.

questions.explanation: The writer rejects the common view (tall buildings, wide roads) and gives his own measure: a good town takes care of its weakest people. "Tall buildings make a town rich and beautiful" is the view the writer does not agree with — the trap of the first sentence. Roads for cars are not his point, and "children, old and sick people" is a detail taken out of his idea.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Nadia saved her pocket money for months. On Saturday she counted her coins on the table, sighed, shook her head and slowly put the bicycle catalogue back on the shelf."

What can we infer from this passage?

options.text: She bought the bicycle that same day.
She no longer liked bicycles.
She did not have enough money yet.
She wanted to buy a new catalogue.

questions.explanation: The clues after the counting — a sigh, a shake of the head, the catalogue back on the shelf — show disappointment: her money is still not enough for the bicycle. "She bought the bicycle that same day" goes against every clue: a happy buyer does not sigh. She saved for months to buy one, so she still likes bicycles.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The school closed for two weeks last winter. Teachers recorded their lessons, and pupils watched them at home. But this solution had one serious limit: pupils with no internet could not follow."

In the third sentence, what does "this solution" refer to?

options.text: the serious limit
the pupils with no internet
closing the school for two weeks
the recorded lessons

questions.explanation: "This solution" points back to the answer the teachers found in the sentence before: the lessons they recorded for pupils to watch at home. Closing the school is the problem, not the solution — the tempting answer, because it is also mentioned before. The limit and the pupils with no internet come after the phrase.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The volunteers worked tirelessly all weekend: they cleaned the beach from morning to night, in the heat, and never stopped for a rest."

What does the word "tirelessly" most probably mean?

options.text: without any pay
without stopping or getting tired
in complete silence, without a word
very slowly and very carefully

questions.explanation: The parts of the word give the meaning — "tire" + "less" + "ly": without getting tired — and the context confirms it: from morning to night, never stopping. "Without any pay" is true of volunteers, but it is not the meaning of this word. "Very slowly" is contradicted by the hard, steady work, and silence is never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Put these sentences in the correct order to form a well-organised paragraph:

1. "That's why many of us now take a cloth bag to the shop."
2. "Plastic bags are a big problem in our town."
3. "They fly in the streets and end up in the sea."
4. "In the sea, turtles eat them because they look like food."

What is the best order?
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 is the general topic sentence, so it opens the paragraph. Sentence 3 follows the bags to the sea, and sentence 4 starts with "In the sea", so it comes after 3. "That's why" (1) sums up all the problems and gives the consequence, so it closes: 2 – 3 – 4 – 1. Putting 4 before 3 sends the bags into the sea before they reach it.

questions.prompt:
Read this paragraph about good manners:

"Good manners cost nothing but bring great rewards. A polite greeting makes people feel respected. Holding the door for others shows kindness. The new shopping centre has a huge car park. That's why small polite acts make life better for everyone."

Which sentence breaks the unity of the paragraph and should be removed?

options.text: "The new shopping centre has a huge car park."
"A polite greeting makes people feel respected."
"Holding the door for others shows kindness."
"That's why small polite acts make life better for everyone."

questions.explanation: The paragraph develops one idea — the value of good manners — with two examples (a greeting, holding the door) and a closing sentence opened by "That's why". The car park of the shopping centre proves nothing about good manners: it is irrelevant and breaks the unity. The closing sentence must stay: it sums up the idea.
